usage: tunnel [-h] [--base BASE] [--json] [--version]
              {serve,status,stop,init,agents,mcp,ls,requests,wait,set,rm,apply,export,pack,reset,mode,session,record,recordings,ssl,check,ca} ...

tunnel: a local proxy and mock server — configure what each endpoint answers,
watch the traffic, replay what was recorded

positional arguments:
  {serve,status,stop,init,agents,mcp,ls,requests,wait,set,rm,apply,export,pack,reset,mode,session,record,recordings,ssl,check,ca}
    serve               start the admin port (127.0.0.1) and the proxy port
    status              whether a background server is running, and where
    stop                stop the server started with `serve --background`
    init                create .tunnel/ here so this project keeps its own
                        config, state and recordings
    agents              print the guide for coding agents, for the version
                        installed
    mcp                 speak MCP on stdin and stdout, so a coding agent
                        drives tunnel with typed tools
    ls                  list the configured mocks
    requests            what the client actually called, aggregated or one by
                        one
    wait                block until the client has made this request (exit 3
                        on timeout)
    set                 configure one endpoint; only the fields you pass
                        change
    rm                  delete one endpoint's rule
    apply               apply a scenario file: a group of mocks, all or
                        nothing
    export              export the configured mocks as a scenario file
    pack                inline a scenario's script_file and json_file, for a
                        test bundle to apply on its own
    reset               clear what one test case leaves for the next
    mode                how endpoints with no rule of their own are answered
    session             the session this run records into and replays from
    record              record the calls that pass through to the real server
    recordings          the recorded calls: list, export, import and delete
                        them
    ssl                 which hosts tunnel decrypts (Charles calls these SSL
                        Proxying Locations)
    check               send one request through the proxy port and print the
                        answer
    ca                  the CA certificate devices install so tunnel can
                        decrypt HTTPS

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --base BASE           where the admin API answers (default
                        http://127.0.0.1:8000)
  --json                print raw JSON, errors included, for piping into jq
  --version             show program's version number and exit
